nodes.label: HOCON configuration
nodes.rationale: A superset of JSON with substitutions, durations and sizes. Three layers resolved highest-first: constructor arguments, user config (application.conf / configFile / inline config), then the bundled reference defaults.

nodes.label: REFERENCE_CONF bundled defaults
nodes.rationale: Layer 1 - the built-in defaults in src/config/reference.ts that anything unspecified falls through to.

nodes.label: application.conf
nodes.rationale: The project-root user config, auto-loaded on ActorSystem.create.

nodes.label: Loading order (six layers)
nodes.rationale: REFERENCE_CONF, application.conf in CWD, the configFile path, the ACTOR_TS_CONFIG env var, an inline config object, then explicit constructor fields which always win for what they cover.

nodes.label: `include` directives are refused
nodes.rationale: A decision, not a gap: resolving an include would let whoever writes the config choose which paths the process reads, relative to a root the parser cannot know. Merging in code (Config.parseFile + merge) leaves that choice with the caller, and the parser says all of this when it meets an include so a config ported from another framework fails with an answer rather than a puzzle.

nodes.label: Reserved keys: __proto__, constructor, prototype
nodes.rationale: A key path is expanded onto a plain object, and assigning __proto__ writes through to the object prototype rather than creating a normal key - allowing it would let a config file change the behaviour of every object in the process. The check is exact-match, so _proto_ and constructorName work normally.

nodes.label: Reads see own keys only
nodes.rationale: Refusing three names guards the write side; the read side is guarded positively instead, because Object.prototype has a dozen more members and a deny list could never keep up. Every substitution, hasPath and typed getter reads own keys only, so ${toString} misses rather than resolving to an inherited member.

nodes.label: remote.tls.enabled is read but not honoured
nodes.rationale: Setting it true buys a startup WARN naming the key and saying the wire is plaintext, so a security setting the framework ignores shows up in logs and not only in the docs (#591); encrypting the transport is #941. The value is strictly type-checked because the forgiving reading of a typo is 'not enabled', which would leave the node on plaintext while the config says TLS. Passing your own transport silences the key entirely.

nodes.label: OptionsError
nodes.rationale: Thrown for a present-but-invalid option value, naming the offending field and what it expected. Distinct from ConfigError and BrokerOptionsError; raised in preStart for broker actors and from the constructor for non-broker consumers.

nodes.label: ConfigError
nodes.rationale: Malformed HOCON - wrong type, missing path.

nodes.label: BrokerOptionsError
nodes.rationale: A required broker setting absent from every layer.

nodes.label: Validation runs once, at consume time, on merged settings
nodes.rationale: Because it runs on the merged result, the same rules apply however a value arrived - fluent builder, plain object, or HOCON key - and cross-field rules see the final values. Unset optionals never trigger it.

nodes.label: A rejected URL is reported with credentials masked
nodes.rationale: Every rule that rejects a URL replaces the userinfo with *** in both the message and OptionsError.value, because a rejected broker URL is logged at ERROR and a password that has reached a log aggregator has to be rotated, not deleted. Nothing else about the value is touched, so a non-URL comes back verbatim.

nodes.label: HOCON durations
nodes.rationale: ns/us/ms/s/m/h/d suffixes; bare numbers parse as numbers, so duration keys require an explicit unit.

nodes.label: HOCON sizes
nodes.rationale: B/K/M/G/T, binary (1024) by default.

nodes.label: Environment substitution
nodes.rationale: ${?ENV} for optional, ${ENV} for required - the way to keep credentials out of a committed application.conf.

nodes.label: actor-ts.cluster keys
nodes.rationale: Gossip and seed-retry intervals, weakly-up, the max-members / max-tombstones caps, the tombstone block and the failure-detector thresholds. The HOCON tree and ClusterOptions are deliberately not isomorphic - tombstone knobs are grouped because that is how you tune them while the fields stay flat - and min-retention = 0s means derive from the failure detector, not no floor.

nodes.label: actor-ts.cluster.pub-sub keys
nodes.rationale: The three caps bound what one mediator can be made to hold and publish fan-out walks all of them, so they are a latency bound as much as a memory one - and max-topics is enforced against gossiped topic claims, not only local subscribes.

nodes.label: actor-ts.distributed-data keys
nodes.rationale: Top-level rather than under cluster.* because the module is - DistributedData ships from src/crdt/ and the cluster is a positional argument to start(). Every pending quorum request holds a promise, a timer and a target set until its deadline, so the caps turn a later timeout storm into immediate rejections that name the knob.

nodes.label: actor-ts.http.client keys
nodes.rationale: A floor, not a policy: per-integration and per-call overrides still win, and what the block buys is moving fleet-wide numbers without a code change. maxResponseBytes and defaultTimeoutMs must be positive here - unlike a request's timeoutMs where 0 opts one call out of any deadline - because a 0 here would disarm every call that named no deadline.

nodes.label: actor-ts.sharding keys
nodes.rationale: Node-wide baselines read once per sharding.start(...) and layered under whatever that call passes, so a per-type setting belongs in the builder. shard-passivation-idle is deliberately absent from reference.conf, because a shipped value is what 'unset' would have to be distinguishable from.

nodes.label: actor-ts.persistence plugin keys
nodes.rationale: The plugin keys are fully-qualified HOCON paths to where that plugin's settings live, not short names - 'sqlite' will not resolve.

nodes.label: Where the built-in default lives
nodes.rationale: Not every setting has a reference.conf key, and even those that do need a code value for when nothing is configured. Options defaults sit next to the field in the matching XOptions.ts; everything else - caps, bounds and timeouts with no option behind them - lives in a Constants.ts. So a leaf and its fallback are always exactly two files, the second named after the first.
